title: Two missionary brothers
hookLine: a nun who never leaves her convent becomes a sister to two young men across the world, and the week comes back
tomorrow: after everything, what were Thérèse's last words?

lines: A JOY SHE WANTED: A BROTHER.
cards: A friend on deployment. A cousin on a mission trip you text at strange hours because of the time zones. A pen pal you've never seen in person.
Every message says the same small thing: you're still mine, even from here. Thérèse never left her convent. And yet, in Manuscript C, she writes about a joy she had wanted for a long time: a brother.
A young man training for the priesthood asked the Carmel for a sister who would pray for him, and the request was handed to her.

teach.b: Later a second one came, a young priest leaving as a missionary. She hesitated. Her prayers were already offered for the first; could she split them?

She decides she can't divide what belongs to Jesus, and gives it all to both. She writes to them as a sister: encouragement, honesty, her little way, sent across the world from inside walls she won't leave.
Prayer was the one thing she could send anywhere, and she sent all of it.

Near the end of the manuscript she takes a line from the Song of Songs, in the Douay-Rheims: "Draw me: we will run after thee." When one soul is drawn to God, she says, the souls it loves come running behind.
Now look back at the week, because every piece was in it. The cross first, waiting just inside the convent door at fifteen. The holy face, seen in her father's hidden years of illness.
The smile, for the sister who grated. A little splash, at the washing tub. Petals, the small sacrifices thrown where nobody saw.
Honest and kind, with the novices.
And now a sister far away: love that crosses an ocean without moving.

how: Some Catholics, especially in religious communities, commit to praying for a particular priest or missionary for years, and the Church honors Thérèse as a patron of missions.

o: two young men Thérèse took as brothers by prayer and letter

two priests who heard confessions at her convent

games.q: two brothers far away — tap the pairs.
p: a priest leaving as a missionary

s: Thérèse traveled as a missionary before she died
she never left Carmel; she was a sister to missionaries by letter and prayer.
she hesitated before taking on a second brother
then decided she couldn't divide what belonged to Jesus, and gave all to both.
she read 'draw me: we will run' as being about one soul alone
she reads it as the souls we love running behind the one who is drawn.

games.q: your grandmother prays every night for a cousin stationed overseas. your brother says it's pointless if he never hears about it. what would Thérèse say?
o: it isn't: she was a sister to two men far away, by prayer and letters.
he's right: prayer only reaches people who know you're praying.
it counts only once the cousin writes back to say thank you.
games.why: Thérèse gave her whole prayer to two brothers across the world and read 'draw me: we will run' as souls running together. distance didn't make it smaller.

practice: Count on your fingers the people far from you who carry you somehow: someone who prays for you, writes to you, thinks of you when you don't know it. One finger each, and a name for every finger.
Then let the sit hold all of them at once.

wordCard.voice: Two missionary brothers. The young men Thérèse wrote to as a sister, from a convent she never left.

orig.note: Latin for sister: what Thérèse became, by letter and prayer, to two men far away.

carryVoice: Your line: a sister far away. Distance doesn't cancel being family. Have a good week.
